html:
From the early 1970s, millions of people from Kerala in south India went to work in the oil states of the Persian Gulf. It is one of the largest labour migrations of modern times; see also Kerala workers to the Gulf.

Kerala had good schools and high literacy but few jobs. When oil prices jumped after the 1973 oil embargo, Gulf states such as Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait began to build fast and needed workers. Keralites went as builders, drivers, nurses, clerks and shop owners, usually alone and on contracts, with no path to citizenship.

The money they sent home changed Kerala. Remittances paid for new houses, schools and hospitals, and became a large share of the state's income. Whole towns came to depend on the Gulf. The risks showed in 1990, when Iraq invaded Kuwait and India flew out about 170,000 of its people in the 1990 airlift, many of them from Kerala.
sum: From the early 1970s, millions of people from Kerala in south India went to work in the oil states of the Persian Gulf. It is one of the largest labour migrations of modern times; see also Kerala workers to the Gulf.
